title: Lightning
summary: Long exposures of a distant storm, safely.

media.alt: Lightning bolts over a harbour and lighthouse at night

blocks.text: **Stay safe.** Shoot from indoors or a car, with the storm well away. If thunder comes less than 30 s after the flash, the storm is close: stop and shelter. Wait 30 minutes after the last thunder before going out.

blocks.note: At night the open shutter waits for the bolt. Brighter town? Shorten the shutter or close the aperture.

steps: Find a window or sheltered spot facing the storm, with a clear view of the sky.
Manual focus on a distant light or the horizon. Lightning is always 'at infinity'.
M mode: f/8, ISO 100, 15 s. Check a test frame isn't too bright from town lights.
Point at the part of the sky with the most strikes and shoot frames back to back with the interval timer.
Keep shooting. Most frames will be empty; that's normal.
Daytime storms: an exposure long enough to catch a bolt needs a dark ND filter, or record 4K video and pull out the frame.

items: A lightning trigger (a sensor on the hot shoe) fires the shutter for you, and is the only easy way to catch bolts by day.
Wide lens first. Once you know where strikes land, zoom in.
An action camera recording video from a window catches strikes too.
